headline: 20 Bangladeshis killed in Russia-Ukraine war after being tricked into fighting
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) revealed that men recruited for construction jobs were forced into the Russian Army and killed in drone strikes.
details: Twenty of 30 Bangladeshis allegedly recruited for construction jobs in Russia have been killed after being forced to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war, according to the Special Response Battalion (SRB).
Seventeen of the victims died in a drone strike on their first day at the front, while three others died later, Additional DIG Asaduzzaman, commander of SRB-10, said in a Dhaka news conference.
The findings emerged during an investigation into a human trafficking case filed by the father of Rajon Hossain, 21, who returned home wounded.

Investigators say a trafficking network, operating with help from contacts in Russia and Kyrgyzstan, recruited young men from nine districts through three companies: Jabal-e-Nur, RS International and TS Group.

Rajon Hossain was allegedly charged Tk 825,000 for a construction job. After arriving in Russia on May 7, he and 30 others were forced into the Russian Army, received 21 days of training and sent to the front.

A drone strike fractured Rajon’s pelvis and fractured his legs, leaving him unable to move. He reportedly crawled nearly four kilometres to reach a camp and spent four days struggling to get to a hospital.
With embassy assistance, Rajon returned to Bangladesh on August 23. Two other returnees are recovering in Bangladesh, while two remain in a Moscow hospital and six are still on the battlefield.
Two alleged recruiters, Mizanur Rahman and Abu Taher Lentu, were arrested on Tuesday. Investigators are continuing to search for other members of the network.

headline: CNG driver injured in cocktail explosion near July Uprising Museum
summary: Two cocktails were thrown on the road in front of the museum in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, leaving one person injured.
details: A CNG auto-rickshaw driver was injured after a cocktail exploded in front of the July Uprising Memorial Museum in the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar area of the capital.
The incident occurred around 10:45 PM on Wednesday night, according to Deputy Commissioner (DC) Ibn Mizan of the DMP's Tejgaon Division.
Police reported that two cocktails were thrown onto the road; one exploded while the other remained unexploded.
The exploding cocktail landed on a CNG auto-rickshaw, causing injuries to the driver, who was immediately sent to the hospital for treatment.
The DMP's Bomb Disposal Unit was called to the scene to neutralize the the unexploded cocktail.
Police have visited the site and are currently reviewing CCTV footage to identify the perpetrators of the attack.
